device_analysis.topology: Two parallel waveguides with directional coupling via evanescent field interaction
device_analysis.function: Power is split between the two output ports based on coupling length and gap spacing
key_characteristics: Two waveguides running parallel to each other
Upper waveguide: width 1.3 um, positioned at y = +0.85 um (center)
Lower waveguide: width 1.3 um, positioned at y = -0.85 um (center)

iterations.issue: Geometry was inverted - curves pointed away from center instead of toward
GDS height still 3.4 um instead of 3 um - gdsfactory was processing geometry unexpectedly

iterations.description: Realized gdsfactory caching issue - bypassed @gf.cell decorator
iterations.issue: Still failing - root cause: waveguides were positioned at ±0.75 with width 0.5, giving only 2 um height total

iterations.description: Breakthrough: realized target fills almost entire 3 um height
iterations.note: Used straight rectangles: top from 0.2 to 1.5 um, gap 0 to 0.4 um, bottom from -1.5 to -0.2 um
Curves had minimal effect at rendering resolution
Tapering also undetectable at rendering resolution; hit iteration limit

final_device.description: Parametric directional coupler with two parallel waveguides
final_device.topology: primitives-only: polygons with computed path points
function_knobs: gap_um: controls coupling strength (smaller gap = stronger coupling)
coupling_length_um: controls interaction length (drives FSR/power split ratio)
wg_width_center_um: controls mode confinement at interaction region
final_device.convergence_note: IoU plateaued at 0.5028 (iteration 4-6 all identical). Below the 0.85 target but above 0.5. The diff image shows remaining red at edges where target has subtle curves; at 88px/um rendering resolution, fine geometric details collapse to the same pixels.
